roundNote: Round 6 tests the migration identifiers folded in from INFRA-537 (plan.md 'Migration numbering', the INFRA-537 spec v2 checklist) and the architect's added point (Envoy c4f2e430, 21:32Z). That point: after the version columns widen from int4 to bigint, show that no prepared or cached read of them fails, including on old pods' open connections during a rolling deploy. The broker stays numbered by the architect's decision, so I do not count that. scripts/conflicts/ and the ci.yaml router are unchanged since a4ca5918 (0 files), so rounds 2-5's proofs of them still apply.

implementerProof.how: I re-ran the implementer's claims with my own Postgres (PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector 0.8.7 on 127.0.0.1:55433, a separate data directory), my own scratch clone and branches, and drivers that call each runner's real entry points (daemon store.Open + Migrate + SchemaVersion/SchemaVersionTx; Dispatch store.Open + Migrate + Pool.Healthy; store.Census), built from main 2b427f930eac, this head 7fcdf0e1, a B-only tree and the merged tree. Every claim of the implementer's held: no conflict in either merge order, each migration recorded once in every order, the duplicate tests fail on a shared timestamp, the census reads both column types. The proof is not wrong; it misses the rolling-deploy case below, which fails.

failures.criterion: After the version columns widen from int4 to bigint, no prepared or cached read of them fails, including old pods' open connections during a rolling deploy (architect, Envoy c4f2e430, 2026-10-29 21:32Z)
failures.evidence: Dispatch's createVersionTable widens schema_migrations.version at every boot of this head, with or without a timestamped migration to record (store.go, 'if dataType == "integer"'), so the first new pod of this merge's roll widens the column while main's pods still serve. Main's Pool.Healthy reads 'select coalesce(max(version), 0) from schema_migrations' uncast on its one health-pool connection (healthPoolSize = 1). Reproduced with main's real code: a main-built process looping Pool.Healthy on a database migrated by main, while a head-built process runs Migrate on it. Output: '21:39:09.940 old-dispatch Healthy=0 err=ERROR: cached plan must not change result type (SQLSTATE 0A000)', one failed read among 20, then 140 again. In production each old pod answers one /healthz with 503 and db:false and logs 'dispatch: health probe failed' (main.go:1318-1323). Readiness needs 3 failures in a row (dispatch_kube.go readyProbe(8766, 10, 3, 3)), so no pod leaves the Service, but any single read of /healthz at that moment fails. The same head-built old process (this head's ::bigint cast) across the merged tree's widening: 10 clean reads, 0 failed. So the cast protects a widening only once the old pods carry it, and widening at a boot with no timestamped migration is what breaks main's pods now. Red test: packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/migrate_out_of_order_test.go TestMigrateWithNoTimestampedMigrationKeepsThePreviousReleasesHealthProbeAnswering, commit 017d1df01dcb. It holds a connection of the store's separate pools, runs main's uncast probe, migrates a set with no timestamped migration, and runs the probe again. Command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:55433/postgres?sslmode=disable go test ./internal/dispatch/store/ -run '^TestMigrateWithNoTimestampedMigrationKeepsThePreviousReleasesHealthProbeAnswering$' -count=1, which fails with 'the previous release's health probe after a boot that applied no timestamped migration: ERROR: cached plan must not change result type (SQLSTATE 0A000)'. A throwaway change in a scratch tree, widening only when the loaded set holds a version above 2147483647 as the daemon already does, turns it green with TestHealthyAnswersAcrossTheWideningOfTheVersionColumn, TestMigrateWidensAnIntegerVersionColumnAndRecordsATimestamp, both out-of-order tests, TestMigrateCreatesEmptySchemaAndIsIdempotent and TestMigrateSkipsVersionRecordedOutsideTheRunner all passing. The fix is the implementer's to choose.

Daemon, not a failure of this pull request: a deployment that skips this release, going from a pre-change daemon straight to a release with its first timestamped migration while the old daemon still holds pool connections, would see main's uncast SchemaVersion fail once per connection, as the old-daemon loop shows. In the normal order this release (with the cast) runs first.

My Postgres instance was initialised with SQL_ASCII, so TestScannedTimestampsCarryUTCWhateverTheHostZone fails on it ('client_encoding=UTF8'). That has nothing to do with this change, and I ran only named tests.
